w-ma-019.title: Moroccan Chicken with Preserved Lemon and Olives

instructions.1: Wash the chicken and cut it into pieces. Place it in a bowl and sprinkle with salt, saffron, ginger, turmeric, black pepper, smen, chopped coriander, and parsley. Mix well and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the oil and sauté the onions until golden brown. Add the garlic, turmeric, and salt, and stir for a minute.
instructions.3: Add the chicken pieces to the pot and stir until they turn golden. Add water to cover the chicken and bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the chicken livers (if using), preserved lemon, and olives. Mix well and let it cook for an additional 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve the chicken hot with rice or Moroccan bread.

w-ma-019.culturalNotes: Moroccan Chicken with Preserved Lemon and Olives is a traditional dish in Moroccan cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-ma-021.title: Seffa Medfouna

instructions.1: Wash the broken vermicelli and drain it. Place it in a large bowl and add 3 tablespoons of oil and 2 teaspoons of salt. Mix well.
instructions.2: Place the broken vermicelli in a colander and drain it well. Place it in a steamer and steam for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: While steaming, soak the raisins in water for 20 minutes.
instructions.4: In another bowl, mix 4 tablespoons of unsalted butter with 1/2 cup of powdered sugar. Mix well and set aside.
instructions.5: In a large pot, melt 4 tablespoons of unsalted butter and 1/4 cup of olive oil. Add the chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
instructions.6: Add the chicken pieces and spices (ginger, salt, white pepper, black pepper, cinnamon sticks, saffron, turmeric). Cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Add 2 cups of water and simmer the chicken on low heat for 45 minutes until cooked.
instructions.8: In a small bowl, mix 1 cup of powdered sugar with 2 tablespoons of ground cinnamon.
instructions.9: After steaming, place the broken vermicelli in a large bowl and add the butter and sugar mixture. Mix well.
instructions.10: Place the broken vermicelli in a serving dish and add the chicken and sweet mixture. Garnish with fried and ground almonds, chopped cilantro, and caramelized raisins (if desired).

w-ma-021.culturalNotes: Seffa Medfouna is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions. It is characterized by its rich spice blend and toasted almonds.

w-ma-029.title: Kebab Maghdour

w-ma-029-i15.name: Eggs
w-ma-029-i15.standardAmount: 3-6 (counting half to a whole egg per person)

w-ma-029-i17.name: Chopped flat leaf parsley or coriander

instructions.1: Prepare the meat by cutting it into 1-inch cubes.
instructions.2: In a bowl, mix the meat with grated onion, garlic, ginger, pepper, parsley and coriander, and vegetable oil. Let the mixture marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: In a pot, add the vegetable and olive oil, then add the finely chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
instructions.4: Add the marinated meat to the pot and sauté for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Add water to cover the meat, then add ginger, salt, cinnamon stick, and ground sweet paprika. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
instructions.6: Add the eggs to the pot and cook for 10 minutes until they are done.
instructions.7: Serve the Kebab Maghdour hot, garnished with chopped parsley.

w-ma-029.culturalNotes: Kebab Maghdour is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions. It is known for its rich spice flavors and tender meat.

w-mx-046.title: Chile Relleno

w-mx-046-i2.name: Monterey Jack cheese
w-mx-046-i2.standardAmount: 8 ounces (cut into long strips or shredded)

instructions.1: Roast the poblano peppers over medium heat until the skin is blackened. Place them in a sealed plastic bag for 10 minutes to cool.
instructions.2: Peel the peppers and cut off the stem. Gently open the peppers and remove the seeds and inner membrane.
instructions.3: Stuff the peppers with Monterey Jack cheese. Set the stuffed peppers aside.
instructions.4: In a bowl, beat the eggs with salt. In another bowl, place the flour.
instructions.5: Dip the stuffed peppers in the flour, then in the beaten eggs.
instructions.6: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Fry the peppers until golden brown on all sides.
instructions.7: Make the tomato sauce by blending the tomatoes, onion, garlic, jalapeño, cilantro, salt, and olive oil in a blender until smooth.
instructions.8: Serve the stuffed peppers with the tomato sauce on the side.

w-mx-046.culturalNotes: Chile relleno is a traditional Mexican dish often served on special occasions.

w-mx-048.title: Mexican Cinnamon Tea

instructions.1: Place the water and cinnamon in a medium-sized saucepan and bring to a boil.
instructions.2: Let it boil for 3-5 minutes, then remove from heat.
instructions.3: Let it steep for an additional 30 minutes or to taste based on desired strength.

w-mx-048.culturalNotes: Mexican cinnamon tea is a traditional drink that is very popular in Mexico, especially during holidays and special occasions.

w-mx-049.title: Fish Fillet with Garlic Sauce

w-mx-049-i4.name: Vegetable oil (or a mix of half olive oil and half vegetable oil)

instructions.1: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Set aside while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over low heat. Once hot, fry the garlic slices until they are golden. Make sure to remove them promptly once they are lightly golden; if you leave them longer, they will get a bitter taste.
instructions.3: If using the flour, dust the fillets with the flour lightly. Then, turn the heat to medium-high on the frying pan where you cooked the garlic. Once hot, add the fish and cook on both sides. The cooking time will depend on the fish’s thickness. It will be about 2-3 minutes per side for those fillets about 1/3 inch thick, and about 5-7 minutes for thicker fillets.
instructions.4: Remove the fish from the frying pan and place it on a cooling rack with paper towel underneath to absorb any excess fat.
instructions.5: Serve the fish garnished with the chopped parsley and golden garlic slices. (And if you add a little dab of butter, oh heavens!)

w-mx-049.culturalNotes: This dish is one of the popular dishes in Mexican cuisine, often served as a main course at family gatherings.

w-mx-050.title: Green Chile and Cheese Quesadilla

instructions.1: Preheat a comal for 1 minute over medium-low heat.
instructions.2: Warm tortillas for 1 minute on one side, flip and sprinkle some of the cheese on one of the tortillas, add chile, and top with another tortilla and press gently with a spatula.
instructions.3: Flip occasionally until quesadillas are golden brown on each side and cheese has melted.
instructions.4: Repeat with remaining tortillas and ingredients.
instructions.5: Top them with salsa and guacamole, if desired.

w-mx-050.culturalNotes: Quesadilla is a popular dish in Mexico, served as a snack or main meal.
